conventions.canonical_side: bullish/long; apply the catalog mirror table for bearish/short
conventions.copy_rule: strategies copy name, kind, plain_definition, numeric_definition and definition_source verbatim; ts is strategy-specific
conventions.level_rule: kind 'level': if value_expr is null the numeric_definition IS the price; otherwise numeric_definition is the validity condition and value_expr the price
conventions.null_numeric: numeric_definition null => not computable; reason in not_computable_reason

signals.name: arjoio_ny_am_session
signals.plain_definition: The presenter's New York AM session: 08:30 to 11:00 New York time.

signals.name: arjoio_ny_pm_session
signals.plain_definition: The presenter's New York PM session: 13:30 to 16:00 New York time.

signals.name: asia_consolidation
signals.plain_definition: The Asian session stays in a tight range without expansion.
signals.numeric_definition: count((bullish_fvg[0].formed OR bearish_fvg[0].formed) AND ny_minute >= 20:00, ny_minute / tf_minutes + 240 / tf_minutes + 1) == 0
signals.notes: Consolidation = no engine FVG in either direction during 20:00-24:00 NY.

signals.name: asia_expansion
signals.plain_definition: The Asian session expands away from the higher-timeframe PD array and leaves fair value gaps in its leg.
signals.numeric_definition: count(bullish_fvg[0].formed AND ny_minute >= 20:00, ny_minute / tf_minutes + 240 / tf_minutes + 1) >= 1
signals.notes: Expansion = at least one engine (displacement) FVG in the trade direction during 20:00-24:00 NY.

signals.name: asian_range_high
signals.plain_definition: Highest price of the Asian session (20:00-24:00 New York) that precedes the current NY day.

signals.name: asian_range_low
signals.plain_definition: Lowest price of the Asian session (20:00-24:00 New York) that precedes the current NY day.

signals.name: breaker_mean_threshold
signals.plain_definition: 50% of the breaker candle body.
signals.notes: Uses the current breaker candle/body, unlike mean_threshold_bodies whose notes assume an order-block candle frozen one bar back.

signals.name: breaker_pattern
signals.plain_definition: A high forms, price then sweeps the prior swing low, and then closes back above that high; the up candle(s) at the broken high form the breaker block.
signals.numeric_definition: swing_low[0].price < swing_low[1].price AND swing_high[0].open_time > swing_low[1].open_time AND swing_high[0].open_time < swing_low[0].open_time AND close > swing_high[0].price AND close[-1] <= swing_high[0].price
signals.notes: Differs from engine subtype 'breaker' (an OB later closed through its far edge).

signals.name: consolidation
signals.plain_definition: Sideways price action with no expansion over a recent window.
signals.numeric_definition: highest(high, K_CONSOLIDATION_CANDLES) - lowest(low, K_CONSOLIDATION_CANDLES) <= K_CONSOLIDATION_RANGE_ATR * atr

signals.name: consolidation_expansion_consolidation
signals.plain_definition: Three-candle rhythm: consolidation (or expansion), an expansion candle that creates a fair value gap, then an unpredictable consolidation candle.
signals.notes: True at the close of the expansion candle (direction-free): the next candle is the low-probability third candle.

signals.name: dealing_range
signals.plain_definition: A price range whose low swept the prior swing low (sell-side) and whose high swept the prior swing high (buy-side).

signals.name: dealing_range_high
signals.plain_definition: The high of the current dealing range.

signals.name: dealing_range_low
signals.plain_definition: The low of the current dealing range.

signals.name: decoupled_market
signals.plain_definition: The 30-year Treasury bond market and the US Dollar are not giving the normal inverse read: they are moving together, or the bond leg is too compressed to trust for bias.
signals.not_computable_reason: Requires bond and dollar symbols plus a discretionary 'consolidating heavily' judgement; the video gives no exact measurement window or threshold.
signals.notes: Would need external.bonds.* and external.dxy.* inputs; the transcript also treats 'consolidating heavily' as part of the same low-probability condition without giving a numeric threshold.

signals.name: displacement_candle
signals.plain_definition: A strong expansion candle in the trade direction.
signals.numeric_definition: close > open AND body >= K_DISPLACEMENT_BODY_MULT * avg(body[-1], K_DISPLACEMENT_LOOKBACK)

signals.name: displacement_reaction
signals.plain_definition: A strong, immediate move away from a swept level (bullish: after sell-side is swept).

signals.name: equilibrium_reversion
signals.plain_definition: Price trades back to the 50% midpoint of the current dual-sweep dealing range.
signals.numeric_definition: custom_signals.dealing_range AND low <= (swing_low[0].price + swing_high[0].price) / 2 AND high >= (swing_low[0].price + swing_high[0].price) / 2
signals.notes: Uses the current dealing-range swings as the Fibonacci anchors because the engine does not store a hand-drawn expansion leg.

signals.name: equities_open_judas
signals.plain_definition: A volatile fake move that sweeps liquidity at the 08:30 or 09:30 New York open on indices.
signals.numeric_definition: structural_event.kind == liquidity_sweep_low AND ((ny_minute >= 08:30 AND ny_minute < 08:30 + K_OPEN_WINDOW_MINUTES) OR (ny_minute >= 09:30 AND ny_minute < 09:30 + K_OPEN_WINDOW_MINUTES))

signals.name: failed_rejection
signals.plain_definition: Price sweeps a level but does not displace away from it immediately, drifting instead.
signals.numeric_definition: count(structural_event.kind == liquidity_sweep_low, K_REACTION_WINDOW_CANDLES + 1) > count(structural_event.kind == liquidity_sweep_low, K_REACTION_WINDOW_CANDLES) AND NOT any(custom_signals.displacement_candle, K_REACTION_WINDOW_CANDLES)
signals.notes: True K candles after a sweep of a low when no displacement candle away from it followed.

signals.name: first_fvg_after_array_tap
signals.plain_definition: The very first fair value gap that forms in the trade direction after price taps the higher-timeframe PD array.
signals.numeric_definition: bullish_fvg[0].formed AND any(custom_signals.htf_pd_array_tap, K_TAP_LOOKBACK_CANDLES) AND count(bullish_fvg[0].formed, K_TAP_LOOKBACK_CANDLES) == 1

signals.name: flod
signals.plain_definition: First line of defense: the first PD array met on a retracement, most often a fair value gap.

signals.name: friday_tgif_reversal
signals.plain_definition: On Friday, price sweeps Thursday's low and closes back above it, producing the TGIF reversal; mirror for bearish.
signals.numeric_definition: ny_dow == 5 AND low <= pdl AND close >= pdl
signals.notes: Uses the previous-day low on Friday, so it must be derived from intraday candles aligned to the New York day.

signals.name: fvg_disrespected
signals.plain_definition: A candle body closes through the fair value gap's far edge (the gap fails).
signals.notes: Identical to the engine transition fvg.filled == true; steps should use the engine signal directly.

signals.name: fvg_respected
signals.plain_definition: Price wicks into the fair value gap without a candle body closing through it.

signals.name: fvg_touched
signals.plain_definition: Price trades into the fair value gap (a touch or sting), without requiring the consequent encroachment.
signals.notes: Engine 'mitigated' needs the CE; this is the presenters' looser touch.

signals.name: fvg_without_displacement
signals.plain_definition: A three-candle bullish fair value gap with a wick gap between candle 1 and candle 3, regardless of displacement size; mirror for bearish.
signals.notes: Captures the presenter's geometry-only definition. The engine's fvg.bullish additionally requires a displacement candle.

signals.name: htf_opposing_pd_array
signals.plain_definition: The opposing higher-timeframe premium array (for longs) that acts as the draw on liquidity.
signals.notes: Most recent unfilled opposing engine FVG on bias_tf; 'nearest above price' is not expressible.

signals.name: htf_pd_array_tap
signals.plain_definition: Price trades into a higher-timeframe discount array (bullish) or premium array (bearish), such as a fair value gap or order block.
signals.numeric_definition: (low <= bullish_fvg[0].gap_high@bias_tf AND high >= bullish_fvg[0].gap_low@bias_tf AND NOT bullish_fvg[0].filled@bias_tf) OR (low <= bullish_ob[0].zone_high@bias_tf AND high >= bullish_ob[0].zone_low@bias_tf AND NOT bullish_ob[0].invalidated@bias_tf)
signals.notes: Proxy limited to the most recent unfilled engine FVG and the most recent non-invalidated engine OB on bias_tf; other PD arrays (breakers, mitigation blocks, old highs/lows) are not covered.

signals.name: htf_range_displacement
signals.plain_definition: A higher-timeframe bullish displacement candle forms a fair value gap completely above the prior consolidation range, ending Seek and Destroy conditions.
signals.numeric_definition: any(custom_signals.pd_array_failure, K_CONSOLIDATION_CANDLES) AND custom_signals.displacement_candle AND bullish_fvg[0].formed AND bullish_fvg[0].gap_low > highest(high[-1], K_CONSOLIDATION_CANDLES)
signals.notes: Canonical bullish side: the new FVG must print entirely above the previous consolidation window; the bearish side is the mirror.

signals.name: intermediate_term_high
signals.plain_definition: A swing high flanked by a lower swing high on its left and a lower swing high on its right.
signals.notes: Evaluated on the most recent swing-high triple only; the engine's backward scan SwingTracker::intermediateTermHigh() is not exposed (detector backlog).

signals.name: intermediate_term_low
signals.plain_definition: A swing low flanked by a higher swing low on its left and a higher swing low on its right.
signals.notes: See intermediate_term_high.

signals.name: intermediate_term_low_stop
signals.plain_definition: The stop reference beyond which no unmitigated 15m or 1h fair value gap remains (the low that covers higher-timeframe imbalances).
signals.numeric_definition: min(swing_low[0].price, bullish_fvg[0].gap_low@15m * (1 - bullish_fvg[0].filled@15m) + swing_low[0].price * bullish_fvg[0].filled@15m, bullish_fvg[0].gap_low@1h * (1 - bullish_fvg[0].filled@1h) + swing_low[0].price * bullish_fvg[0].filled@1h)
signals.notes: Uses the most recent 15m and 1h FVG only; the presenter picks the swing extreme beyond all such gaps.

signals.name: judas_reversal_zone_tap
signals.plain_definition: An opening Judas swing reaches the first line of defense, usually a bullish fair value gap, or sweeps the last line of defense and closes back above it.
signals.numeric_definition: custom_signals.opening_judas_swing AND ((custom_signals.flod AND low <= custom_signals.flod AND NOT bullish_fvg[0].filled) OR (low <= custom_signals.llod AND close >= custom_signals.llod))
signals.notes: The first-line branch uses the presenter's FVG touch semantics, not the engine's CE mitigation requirement; the last-line branch models a sweep/reclaim of the origin swing low.

signals.name: judas_swing
signals.plain_definition: The manipulation leg: an initial fake move away from the opening price, opposite to the real move, before the expansion.
signals.numeric_definition: lowest(low, ny_minute / tf_minutes + 1) < custom_signals.midnight_open AND close > custom_signals.midnight_open
signals.notes: Fixed to the daily (NY midnight) scale; session/weekly/monthly scales need their own opening price (open question).

signals.name: liquidity_run_continuation
signals.plain_definition: A bullish BOS displacement leaves a bullish fair value gap across the broken high, and the retracement respects that gap for continuation.
signals.numeric_definition: count(structural_event.kind == bullish_bos AND custom_signals.displacement_candle AND bullish_fvg[0].formed AND bullish_fvg[0].gap_low <= structural_event.reference_price AND bullish_fvg[0].gap_high >= structural_event.reference_price, K_REACTION_WINDOW_CANDLES) >= 1 AND custom_signals.fvg_respected
signals.notes: Canonical bullish side. Uses BOS instead of liquidity_sweep_high because the engine sweep detector fires on any breach; the continuation reading needs displacement plus acceptance above the broken high.

signals.name: liquidity_void
signals.plain_definition: A complete gap in price delivery: the candle's whole range lies above the previous candle's range (no overlap of wicks); mirror for bearish.
signals.notes: Presenter: neither buy-side nor sell-side liquidity was delivered, so the ranges do not touch (a candle that merely opens beyond the previous range but trades back into it delivered liquidity). Measured on stored 15m data, both sides: 17 of 176,728 BNBUSDT, 76 of 27,883 XAUUSDT, 9 of 24,887 XAGUSDT candles; mostly TradFi perps around market closures.

signals.name: llod
signals.plain_definition: Last line of defense: the swing extreme at the origin of the current price leg.

signals.name: london_kz_entry_trigger
signals.plain_definition: In the London kill zone: if Asia expanded in the trade direction, any new fair value gap in the trade direction; if Asia consolidated, the second fair value gap of the ST model.
signals.numeric_definition: kill_zone == london AND ((custom_signals.asia_expansion AND bullish_fvg[0].formed) OR (custom_signals.asia_consolidation AND custom_signals.st_model))

signals.name: london_missed_htf_poi
signals.plain_definition: The London session fails to tap the intended higher-timeframe PD array objective.
signals.numeric_definition: kill_zone == new_york_am AND count(custom_signals.htf_pd_array_tap AND kill_zone == london, ny_minute / tf_minutes + 1) == 0
signals.notes: Evaluated during the New York AM session from intraday candles since NY midnight. Encodes only the missed-array condition; the separate claim that London did not make the day's extreme stays descriptive.

signals.name: london_open_price
signals.plain_definition: The opening price at 02:00 New York time (start of the London kill zone).
signals.notes: Valid when ny_minute >= 02:00.

signals.name: london_taps_htf_poi_and_displaces
signals.plain_definition: The London session reaches the higher-timeframe PD array and displaces in the intended trend direction.
signals.numeric_definition: kill_zone == new_york_am AND count(custom_signals.first_fvg_after_array_tap AND kill_zone == london, ny_minute / tf_minutes + 1) >= 1
signals.notes: Evaluated during the New York AM session from intraday candles since NY midnight. Uses the first same-direction FVG after the higher-timeframe tap as the displacement proxy.

signals.name: major_expansion_dol_swept
signals.plain_definition: A major expansion has just taken out the higher-timeframe draw on liquidity.
signals.notes: Evaluated on bias_tf: a displacement candle that sweeps a swing high (buy-side) for longs; the presenter's 'obvious draw' itself is discretionary.

signals.name: manipulation_leg_extreme
signals.plain_definition: The extreme of the manipulation (Judas) leg: the lowest price traded below the opening price before the real move (bullish).

signals.name: market_maker_curve_shift
signals.plain_definition: Price taps a higher-timeframe discount array and then prints a bullish structure shift on the setup timeframe, starting the buy curve of the market maker model.
signals.numeric_definition: custom_signals.htf_pd_array_tap AND (structural_event.kind == bullish_choch OR structural_event.kind == bullish_bos)
signals.notes: Proxy for the presenter’s market maker model transition; the full two-curve profile itself is not separately detected.

signals.name: mb_fvg_overlap_sensitivity
signals.plain_definition: If the mitigation-block wick overlaps a bullish fair value gap, the broken swing high is the entry level; otherwise the swing-high candle body open is.
signals.numeric_definition: (bullish_fvg[0].gap_high >= open[-((open_time - swing_high[0].open_time) / (tf_minutes * 60000))] AND bullish_fvg[0].gap_low <= custom_signals.swing_failure_pattern AND NOT bullish_fvg[0].filled) * custom_signals.swing_failure_pattern + (1 - (bullish_fvg[0].gap_high >= open[-((open_time - swing_high[0].open_time) / (tf_minutes * 60000))] AND bullish_fvg[0].gap_low <= custom_signals.swing_failure_pattern AND NOT bullish_fvg[0].filled)) * open[-((open_time - swing_high[0].open_time) / (tf_minutes * 60000))]
signals.notes: Uses the most recent swing high's wick/body geometry on the bullish canonical side; body-open reconstruction comes from the swing-high candle in price history.

signals.name: mean_threshold_bodies
signals.plain_definition: 50% of the bodies of the order block candle(s), ignoring the wicks.
signals.notes: Frozen at the candle where the block-defining step is satisfied; the block candle is the candle before it (single-candle form; consecutive same-colour candles grouped into one block are not reproduced).

signals.name: measured_swing_projection
signals.plain_definition: A Fibonacci projection family drawn from a Judas Swing back to its opening-price anchor; the presenter uses the exact levels -0.27, -0.68, -1.0, -1.62, and -2.0 depending on which one overlaps the intended PD array.
signals.not_computable_reason: The presenter states a family of exact Fibonacci targets, but the active opening anchor, the wick-vs-body anchor choice, and the chosen target ratio remain discretionary at evaluation time.
signals.notes: The lesson selects among several exact projection levels and allows wick-to-wick or body-to-body anchors across London, daily, weekly, and monthly opening-price profiles. Without one machine-bound opening anchor, one machine-bound Judas-swing leg, and one machine-bound chosen ratio, this signal cannot collapse to a single price.

signals.name: midnight_open
signals.plain_definition: The opening price at 00:00 New York time of the current NY day.
signals.notes: Not available from 1d candles: Binance daily candles open at 00:00 UTC.

signals.name: mitigation_block_pd_array_overlap
signals.plain_definition: The swing-failure-pattern mitigation level lies inside a bullish fair value gap or bullish order block on the same timeframe.
signals.numeric_definition: (custom_signals.swing_failure_pattern >= bullish_fvg[0].gap_low AND custom_signals.swing_failure_pattern <= bullish_fvg[0].gap_high AND NOT bullish_fvg[0].filled) OR (custom_signals.swing_failure_pattern >= bullish_ob[0].zone_low AND custom_signals.swing_failure_pattern <= bullish_ob[0].zone_high AND NOT bullish_ob[0].invalidated)
signals.notes: Overlap partner proxy is limited to bullish FVGs and bullish engine order blocks; breaker-block and other PD-array partners remain outside this signal.

signals.name: monthly_open
signals.plain_definition: The opening price at the start of the month in New York time.
signals.not_computable_reason: Grammar has no NY day-of-month identifier (only ny_minute, ny_dow); data is available, the expression language is not.
signals.notes: Binance 1mo candles open 00:00 UTC on the 1st, not NY time.

signals.name: ny_taps_htf_poi
signals.plain_definition: The New York session reaches the higher-timeframe PD array, completing the objective London missed.
signals.notes: Uses the engine's fixed new_york_am kill zone (07:00-10:00 NY) because this lesson does not state a different presenter-specific window.

signals.name: ob_fvg_overlap_sensitivity
signals.plain_definition: If the order block's wick overlaps a fair value gap, the wick extreme is the entry level; otherwise the body open is.
signals.numeric_definition: (bullish_fvg[0].gap_high >= open[-1] AND bullish_fvg[0].gap_low <= high[-1]) * high[-1] + (1 - (bullish_fvg[0].gap_high >= open[-1] AND bullish_fvg[0].gap_low <= high[-1])) * open[-1]
signals.notes: Frozen at the block-defining step (block candle = t-1); booleans are 1/0 in arithmetic.

signals.name: objective_reached
signals.plain_definition: Price has already tapped the higher-timeframe PD array before 08:30 New York time.

signals.name: obvious_draw_on_liquidity
signals.plain_definition: A higher-timeframe target that is recognisable within about 10 seconds of opening the chart.
signals.not_computable_reason: Discretionary (a 10-second visual judgement); no numeric proxy is defensible.

signals.name: opening_judas_swing
signals.plain_definition: A counter-trend manipulation leg trades below the London session open, below the New York midnight open during the New York AM session, or below the Monday open, then closes back above that opening price.
signals.numeric_definition: (kill_zone == london AND ny_minute >= 02:00 AND lowest(low, ((ny_minute - 02:00) / tf_minutes) + 1) < custom_signals.london_open_price AND close > custom_signals.london_open_price) OR (kill_zone == new_york_am AND custom_signals.judas_swing) OR (lowest(low, (((ny_dow - 1) * 1440 + ny_minute) / tf_minutes) + 1) < custom_signals.weekly_open AND close > custom_signals.weekly_open)
signals.notes: Uses the registry's London, daily, and weekly opening-price proxies; the transcript does not give a separate non-equity New York AM opening price beyond the daily open context.

signals.name: overlapping_pd_array
signals.plain_definition: A fair value gap that shares price with another PD array (order block) on the same timeframe; the shared range is the entry zone.
signals.numeric_definition: max(bullish_fvg[0].gap_low, bullish_ob[0].zone_low) <= min(bullish_fvg[0].gap_high, bullish_ob[0].zone_high) AND NOT bullish_fvg[0].filled AND NOT bullish_ob[0].invalidated
signals.notes: value_expr = first-touch edge of the overlap on a retracement (top for longs); partners limited to engine OBs; breaker/mitigation-block partners need the custom breaker_pattern / swing_failure_pattern levels.

signals.name: pd_array_failure
signals.plain_definition: After price returns to equilibrium, premium or discount arrays stop producing follow-through fair value gaps and price behaves as consolidation.
signals.numeric_definition: any(custom_signals.equilibrium_reversion, K_REACTION_WINDOW_CANDLES) AND custom_signals.consolidation AND count(fvg.formed, K_REACTION_WINDOW_CANDLES) == 0
signals.notes: Wick-heavy candles and 'no follow-through' are proxied by consolidation plus the absence of any new fair value gap inside the reaction window.

signals.name: pre_major_news
signals.plain_definition: The part of a CPI, FOMC or NFP release day before the release time.

signals.name: presenter_order_block
signals.plain_definition: A down candle (or run of consecutive down candles) coming off support whose high is subsequently broken; mirror for bearish.
signals.notes: Covers the single-candle form broken by the next candle; 'coming off support' is not encoded. Looser than the engine OB, which also needs a same-direction FVG and BOS.

signals.name: prior_session_expansion
signals.plain_definition: An earlier session in the same New York day already displaced in the trade direction and left at least one fair value gap, so the next session is less likely to fully retrace and sweep it.
signals.numeric_definition: (kill_zone == london AND count(bullish_fvg[0].formed AND ny_minute >= 20:00, ny_minute / tf_minutes + 240 / tf_minutes + 1) >= 1) OR (kill_zone == new_york_am AND count(bullish_fvg[0].formed AND (ny_minute >= 20:00 OR ny_minute < 07:00), ny_minute / tf_minutes + 240 / tf_minutes + 1) >= 1)
signals.notes: Bullish-side proxy: London checks for an Asian-session displacement FVG; New York checks for an Asian or London displacement FVG before 07:00. 'Strong expansion' is proxied by at least one engine fair value gap in the trade direction.

signals.name: pure_sweep
signals.plain_definition: Price trades through a swing low (sell-side liquidity) and the sweeping candle closes back above it (turtle soup).

signals.name: quadrant_extreme
signals.plain_definition: Price reaches the lowest quarter of the established range (0 to 0.25, discount of discount) for longs.

signals.name: reclaimed_pd_array_overlap
signals.plain_definition: The reclaimed bullish order block overlaps a newly formed right-curve PD array: a bullish fair value gap, a later bullish order block, a breaker pattern level, or a swing-failure-pattern mitigation level.
signals.numeric_definition: (bullish_fvg[0].confirmed_at > order_block.anchor_at AND max(order_block.zone_low, bullish_fvg[0].gap_low) <= min(order_block.zone_high, bullish_fvg[0].gap_high) AND NOT bullish_fvg[0].filled) OR (bullish_ob[0].anchor_at > order_block.anchor_at AND max(order_block.zone_low, bullish_ob[0].zone_low) <= min(order_block.zone_high, bullish_ob[0].zone_high) AND NOT bullish_ob[0].invalidated) OR (custom_signals.breaker_pattern >= order_block.zone_low AND custom_signals.breaker_pattern <= order_block.zone_high) OR (custom_signals.swing_failure_pattern >= order_block.zone_low AND custom_signals.swing_failure_pattern <= order_block.zone_high)
signals.notes: Breaker and mitigation-block partners are proxied by the breaker_pattern and swing_failure_pattern level signals; later order-block partners must form after the reclaimed block’s anchor.

signals.name: reclaimed_trade_through
signals.plain_definition: Price closes back above the high of the left-curve bullish order block, reclaiming it as support on the buy curve.
signals.notes: Uses the bullish order block bound earlier in the strategy steps; bearish examples are the mirror.

signals.name: rejection_block
signals.plain_definition: An outsider candle at a swing extreme with a long wick; price later sweeps the bodies inside the wick but not the wick extreme.
signals.notes: Identification reuses the engine Rejection subtype (swing pivot, wick >= K_REJECTION_WICK_FRACTION of range).

signals.name: rejection_block_body_sweep
signals.plain_definition: Price trades into the rejection block's wick (sweeping the bodies) without taking out the wick extreme.
signals.numeric_definition: low < order_block.zone_high AND low >= order_block.zone_low AND order_block.subtype == rejection

signals.name: relatively_stronger_pair
signals.plain_definition: Among correlated instruments, this chart is the preferred long when it expands further in the bullish direction or holds a swing low that the peer sweeps; for shorts, mirror it to the relatively weaker pair.
signals.not_computable_reason: Requires cross-symbol comparison plus presenter-defined 'more explosive move' / 'fails to break the swing' logic across an arbitrary peer set.
signals.notes: Would need external.correlated.* inputs and, for basket comparisons such as ES/NQ/YM, more than one peer symbol. The transcript does not fix a numeric lookback or a single strength metric.

signals.name: setup_tf_pd_array_tap
signals.plain_definition: Price trades into the 1-hour or 15-minute boundary used for lower-timeframe execution, such as a fair value gap or order block.
signals.numeric_definition: (low <= bullish_fvg[0].gap_high@setup_tf AND high >= bullish_fvg[0].gap_low@setup_tf AND NOT bullish_fvg[0].filled@setup_tf) OR (low <= bullish_ob[0].zone_high@setup_tf AND high >= bullish_ob[0].zone_low@setup_tf AND NOT bullish_ob[0].invalidated@setup_tf)
signals.notes: Proxy limited to the most recent unfilled engine FVG and the most recent non-invalidated engine OB on setup_tf; the daily strong-vs-weak FVG read stays separate context.

signals.name: short_term_high
signals.plain_definition: A standard swing high (three-candle rule) that is not an intermediate term high.
signals.notes: Every confirmed swing high is a short-term high when confirmed; it can only become an ITH once a later lower swing high forms.

signals.name: short_term_low
signals.plain_definition: A standard swing low (three-candle rule) that is not an intermediate term low.

signals.name: short_term_range
signals.plain_definition: A directional swing (swing low to swing high for longs) containing a fair value gap that has not been closed through and holds price on pullbacks.
signals.numeric_definition: swing_high[0].open_time > swing_low[0].open_time AND bullish_fvg[0].confirmed_at > swing_low[0].open_time AND NOT bullish_fvg[0].filled
signals.notes: value_expr = the protected low that started the range (stop reference).

signals.name: short_term_swing_point
signals.plain_definition: The short-term swing point that forms inside the tapped boundary before the new entry fair value gap prints.
signals.notes: Canonical bullish side uses the newly confirmed swing low on the entry timeframe; the bearish side mirrors to swing_high[0].formed.

signals.name: smt_divergence
signals.plain_definition: Between two correlated instruments, one makes a lower swing low while the other makes a higher swing low (crack in correlation).

signals.name: st_model
signals.plain_definition: Displacement, retracement, displacement: a first FVG forms, price retraces into it without closing through it, then a second same-direction FVG forms; entry is on the second.
signals.numeric_definition: bullish_fvg[0].formed AND bullish_fvg[1].confirmed_at >= open_time - K_ST_MAX_CANDLES * (tf_minutes * 60000) AND lowest(low[-1], (open_time - bullish_fvg[1].confirmed_at) / (tf_minutes * 60000) - 1) <= bullish_fvg[1].gap_high AND NOT bullish_fvg[1].filled
signals.notes: 'Retrace into it' = any wick into the first gap (presenter touch), not the engine CE mitigation.

signals.name: standard_deviations
signals.plain_definition: A Fibonacci projection family for indices and futures that uses exact 0.5 increments: -0.5, -1.0, -1.5, -2.0, -2.5, and -3.0.
signals.not_computable_reason: The presenter gives exact ratios, but the signal is a discretionary family of possible targets rather than one single computable price at evaluation time.
signals.notes: The lesson treats these as a menu of targets selected by whichever standard-deviation level overlaps the intended PD array; the active profile anchor and chosen level are not frozen by one engine object.

signals.name: swing_failure_pattern
signals.plain_definition: A low, a high, a higher low (the low is not swept), then a close above that high; the broken high is the mitigation block.
signals.numeric_definition: swing_low[0].price > swing_low[1].price AND swing_high[0].open_time > swing_low[1].open_time AND swing_high[0].open_time < swing_low[0].open_time AND close > swing_high[0].price AND close[-1] <= swing_high[0].price

signals.name: swing_rate_050
signals.plain_definition: The 50% equilibrium swing-rate level between the origin intermediate-term low and the terminus intermediate-term high.
signals.notes: Canonical bullish side; bearish examples mirror the anchors.

signals.name: swing_rate_050_behavior
signals.plain_definition: Price trades at the 50% swing-rate level and shows the deeper-retracement behavior the presenter expects there: consolidation and/or a liquidity sweep before 0.75 is reached.
signals.numeric_definition: (low <= custom_signals.swing_rate_050 AND high >= custom_signals.swing_rate_050) AND (custom_signals.consolidation OR any(structural_event.kind == liquidity_sweep_low, K_REACTION_WINDOW_CANDLES))
signals.notes: Uses the exact presenter 0.5 level, while consolidation and the 'immediate' sweep window are proxied with existing registry constants.

signals.name: swing_rate_075
signals.plain_definition: The 75% swing-rate level between the origin intermediate-term low and the terminus intermediate-term high.
signals.notes: Canonical bullish side; this is the shallow-entry quartile nearest the terminus.

signals.name: swing_rates_framework
signals.plain_definition: An intermediate-term low and the opposing intermediate-term high are established so the 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75 and 1.0 swing rates can be drawn between them.
signals.notes: Canonical bullish side: the origin is the intermediate-term low and the terminus is the intermediate-term high; bearish examples use the mirror table.

signals.name: two_consecutive_fvgs
signals.plain_definition: Two consecutive fair value gaps in the trade direction with no opposite gap between them; entry on the second.

signals.name: unicorn_overlap
signals.plain_definition: A breaker block overlaps a fair value gap on the same timeframe.
signals.numeric_definition: custom_signals.breaker_pattern AND close >= open AND max(bullish_fvg[0].gap_low, open) <= min(bullish_fvg[0].gap_high, high) AND NOT bullish_fvg[0].filled
signals.notes: Canonical bullish side: the breaker block is the current up candle that closes back above the prior swing high; overlap is tested against that candle's range. Distinct from engine order_block.breaker.

signals.name: volume_imbalance
signals.plain_definition: Two consecutive candles whose bodies do not overlap by more than the engine's same-price tolerance while their wicks do.
signals.numeric_definition: min(open, close) - max(open[-1], close[-1]) > K_EQUAL_LEVEL_ATR * atr[-1] AND low <= high[-1]
signals.notes: Presenter geometry: a gap between candle 1's close and candle 2's open with overlapping wicks. Without a tolerance it fires on tick-size gaps (measured on 15m, bullish side: 12,480 of 176,728 BNBUSDT candles); the tolerance reuses the engine's equal-level ATR multiple so that open == previous close counts as the same price. With it: 2 BNBUSDT, 192 XAUUSDT, 299 XAGUSDT 15m candles.

signals.name: weekly_open
signals.plain_definition: The opening price at Monday 00:00 New York time of the current week.
signals.notes: Binance 1w candles open Monday 00:00 UTC, i.e. 4-5 h earlier.
